title: feat: let prompt agents call client tools
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds caller-defined function tools to prompt agents alongside their configured server-side MCP tools.
- Reuses the existing SDK loop: MCP tools execute on the server; caller calls return for client execution. Replay calls and results, including plain-text results, to continue through Responses or Chat Completions.
- Preserves MCP namespace ownership, usage checks and step limits. No new endpoints, storage, dependencies or custom loop; only default/auto tool selection is supported.
- Verified 144 Gen tests, 24 code-agent regressions, 2 Worker SDK tests, Gen typecheck and Biome; independent review found no blockers. No deployment or paid requests.
- Related #14305 (hosted/remote MCP tools remain separate); follows #14454 and #14527.

gist.headline: Tools on both sides
gist.blurb: Prompt agents can now ask your app to use its own tools while MCP tools stay on the server. Everyone keeps their own toolbox.
gist.summary: Prompt agents now accept caller-defined function tools alongside server-side MCP tools, replaying client-executed calls and plain-text results through Responses or Chat Completions using the existing SDK loop.
gist.impact: Developers can execute returned tool calls in their clients and send results back to continue the agent, with MCP namespace ownership, usage checks, and step limits preserved; tool selection supports default/auto mode.
gist.visual_concept: A friendly tool handoff: Polli passes a tiny wrench-shaped function-call card to a client-side CRT robot, while MCP tools remain on a separate server-side workbench. Code-plants connect the two without mixing their toolboxes.
